person_made_it: Built in twenty minutes from Gordon's own complaint (the compare button led to the workshop room) and from Naughty Dog's article: each station pairs one of Astra's six HBO trailer frames with one Naughty Dog image, chosen by eye for the environment they share.
emcee_who_is_speaking: The Look-for line is Gordon's prompt at the podium; the creators' quotes are held behind a Reveal so Druckmann, Pangilinan and Wilson only speak when a student opens them; the status line is the room's stage manager.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Late morning in SCI L104 with the projector on: the same dark teal edit-bay as the lab and the comparison page, so the room does not change when the page does.
did_the_click_pay_me: Every station click records your order and names the place; Directed sequence takes the choice away for twelve seconds a station and says so at the end; Show all six lays the whole deck out for scrolling.
works_for_the_recipient: Phone and projector widths both fit, scripts off shows all six stations stacked with captions, and a blocked Naughty Dog CDN degrades to a labeled archive link rather than a broken box.
taught_me_something: The two versions differ most where nature is allowed in: the QZ removes every plant on purpose and Bill's Town lets it back, and the series frames are almost all green; that contrast is the exercise.
told_me_the_truth: Every pair is labeled as the same world and not the same scene; series frames carry their timecodes; game-side images are credited to the Naughty Dog article with the live and archived links; nothing is presented as a matched shot.
weakest: The pairs are chosen by resemblance, not by matched scene, so a student can be misled into comparing composition when only the world is shared; a Gordon-verified matched pair per station would fix it.
